note: Ps45 royal wedding song (corrected method). Human IB: psalmist's overflowing lev heart, the king's moral inner life (chen grace, aheb loved-righteousness / sane hated-wickedness, sason/samach gladness - Heb1:9), the bride's inner acts (shakach forget her people, avah king desires, shachah bow). Outward glory (hod/hadar splendour/majesty, awesome-deeds) = standalone (not inner operations). 2 God-acts (barak blessed / mashach anointed) = qualifiers. Every candidate roled.

dims.v: 'My HEART (lev) overflows with a pleasing theme' — the inspired heart bubbling over into song; lev here the seat welling up with a good word for the king, the poet's tongue like a ready scribe's pen
the theme the heart overflows with
'a PLEASING (tov) theme' — the goodly matter that stirs the heart to song; tov here the excellence of the subject (the king) that moves the poet's heart to overflow
the graciousness for which God blessed him

'GRACE (chen) is poured upon your lips' — the king's gracious, winsome speech; chen = favour/charm, the gracious character expressed in his words, for which God has blessed him forever (the blessing = qualifier)

'ride out victoriously for the cause of TRUTH (emeth) and meekness and righteousness' — the moral cause the king champions; emeth here the truth his rule advances, the first of the triad of virtues he rides to establish

'the cause of truth and MEEKNESS (anvah) and righteousness' — humility as a royal virtue the king advances; anvah (recurs Ps18:35 'your gentleness') here the meekness/gentleness the warrior-king rides for, the surprising heart of true kingship
'and RIGHTEOUSNESS (tsedeq)' — the justice the king establishes; tsedeq the third of the virtues his victorious ride advances, the moral programme of his reign (echoed in v7's love of righteousness)

'you have LOVED (aheb) righteousness and hated wickedness' — the king's moral affections, the ground of his anointing; aheb here the love of the right that, with hatred of evil, defines his heart (quoted of the Son, Heb1:9)
the object of the king's love
'you have loved RIGHTEOUSNESS (tsedeq)' — the right the king cherishes; tsedeq (recurs v4) here the object of his love, the moral order his heart is set on

'and HATED (sane) wickedness' — the king's moral aversion to evil; sane here the righteous hatred (as Ps26:5) that is the necessary counterpart to loving righteousness, the two-sided moral affection God rewards with anointing
the object of the king's hatred
'and HATED WICKEDNESS (resha)' — the evil the king abhors; resha here the object of his righteous hatred, the moral opposite his heart rejects

'God has anointed you with the oil of GLADNESS (sason) above your companions' — the joy conferred on the righteous-loving king; sason the festal gladness of his anointing (God's anointing = the qualifier), his joy surpassing his fellows'

'From ivory palaces stringed instruments make you GLAD (samach)' — the king gladdened by festal music; samach (recurs widely) the joy of the wedding-day, the king delighted amid myrrh-fragrant robes and music
so the king will desire her beauty

'Hear, O daughter... FORGET (shakach) your people and your father's house' — the bride's inward leaving of her old ties; shakach here the deliberate forsaking of former loyalties to cleave to the king, the cost and turn of covenant union
drawn by her leaving her people
'and the king will DESIRE (avah) your beauty' — the king's longing for the bride; avah (recurs Ps132) the strong desire that answers her self-forgetting, the mutual drawing of the royal marriage

'Since he is your lord, BOW (shachah) to him' — the bride's homage to the king; shachah (recurs Ps29:2 of worship) here the reverent submission owed to her lord, the posture of the queen toward the king
the people of Tyre / the rich
'The people of Tyre will SEEK your favour (chalah) with gifts' — the nations courting the queen; chalah = to entreat/soften the face, the wealthy suing for the favour of the honoured bride
joy / gladness (simchah - with joy and gladness)

'With joy and GLADNESS (simchah) they are led along as they enter the palace' — the festal joy of the wedding procession; simchah the gladness of the bride and her companions entering the king's house, the climax of the celebration
remember / make remembered (zakar, hiphil - your name)
the king's name, in all generations

'I will cause your name to be REMEMBERED (zakar) in all generations' — the poet's vow to perpetuate the king's renown; zakar (hiphil) the making-remembered of the king's name, so the nations praise him forever

'therefore nations will PRAISE (yadah) you forever and ever' — the perpetual acclaim of the king; yadah here the praise of the peoples for the king whose name the poet immortalises, the royal song's enduring end
the blessing following the king's grace (v2)
v2 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'therefore God has BLESSED (barak) you forever' - God's blessing is not a human IB char; it is the divine favour resting on the king's graciousness (278942). Qualifier.
the anointing that confers the king's gladness (v7)

v7 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'God, your God, has ANOINTED (mashach) you with the oil of gladness' - God's anointing is not a human IB char; it is the divine act conferring the king's gladness (278994), his reward for loving righteousness. Qualifier.
v1 superscription/theme: 'a LOVE song (yedidut)' - the genre/character of the psalm (a song of loves for the royal wedding); a designation of the song, not an inner operation. Standalone.

v3: 'in your SPLENDOUR (hod) and majesty' - the king's outward regal glory/magnificence; an attribute of kingly bearing, not an inner operation (per the inner-being focus, glory-words are not characteristics). Standalone.
v3: 'in your splendour and MAJESTY (hadar)' - the king's outward royal glory; an attribute of bearing, not an inner operation. Standalone.
majesty (hadar - in your majesty ride out)
v4: 'In your MAJESTY (hadar) ride out victoriously' - the king's outward glory as he rides; an attribute of bearing, not an inner operation. Standalone.
v4: 'let your right hand teach you AWESOME deeds (yare)' - the fearful/mighty exploits of the king's hand; outward deeds of war, not an inner operation. Standalone.
heart (lev - of the king's enemies, pierced)

v5: 'Your arrows are sharp in the HEART (lev) of the king's enemies' - the heart here as the anatomical target the arrows pierce (the foes fall); a physical target, not an inner operation of the psalmist/king. Standalone.
v2: 'God has blessed you FOREVER (olam)' - the duration of the blessing (278947); a time-word. Standalone.
v6: 'Your throne, O God, is FOREVER (olam) and ever' - the eternity of the throne; a time-word describing the kingdom's endurance, not an inner operation. Standalone.
v8: 'your ROBES (beged) are all fragrant with myrrh' - the king's garments; outward apparel, not an inner operation. Standalone.

v10: 'HEAR (shama), O daughter, and consider, and incline your ear' - the summons to attention preceding the bride's charge to forget her people (278887); the call to listen. Standalone (the IB movement is the forgetting/turning).
joy / rejoicing (gil - with joy and gladness)

v15: 'With JOY (gil) and gladness they are led' - the joy paired with the gladness (278924) of the wedding procession; captured with the gladness char. Standalone (the simchah 278924 carries the IB finding).
v17: 'I will cause your NAME (shem) to be remembered' - the king's name/renown, the object of the remembering (278930); a name, not an inner operation. Standalone.
v17: 'nations will praise you FOREVER (olam) and ever' - the perpetuity of the praise (278935); a time-word. Standalone.
